title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Dungeon Practice 2
content: I wondered what the purpose of this magic circle was. In the Edward route, it was activated by Alicia's scheme, while in other routes, it was triggered by the blunders of the protagonists or target characters.

After walking a short distance along the long, straight path from the teleportation magic circle, we arrived at an open area that resembled an ancient temple, where a massive door loomed in the back, guarded by a Mithril Giant.
It seemed as if it was either protecting something or waiting for someone.
Once we defeated the Mithril guardian, the door opened on its own, revealing a pedestal inside that held a pendant, said to be one of the Holy Artifacts.

At first, it was merely recognized as a valuable pendant, and with lines like, "This is a gift for you, who healed me. It will definitely suit you," it was presented to the protagonist by each of the target characters.
Its true value would only be revealed at the story's climax, when a disaster struck and the Royal Capital faced a crisis, causing one of the Holy Artifacts to shine and grant the protagonist power.

Depending on the target character, there were episodes involving the collection of other Holy Artifacts, and the number required for completion varied, but in the Edward route, just this pendant was sufficient.
"Did I, perhaps, do something bad?"
"Yeah, probably... no, I definitely think it's not good..."
As we walked down the straight path without any destination after teleporting, Alicia sighed, pressing her forehead as she looked at Mariana, who was tilting her head in confusion.
Hmm, that was too careless.
I had no idea there would be a teleportation trap in such a place, but I suppose that's just how it is for a former protagonist.
"This place has a different kind of wall than the first one..."
"Hey! No pickaxes allowed! Throw away anything you've chipped off!"
"Ah, Alicia! Not that! Just that!"
Mariana was still trying to chip away at the wall at this point, so Alicia quickly snatched it away and scolded her.
"Ugh, I thought I could make a groundbreaking discovery..."
"First, your safety! If we can't go back, you won't be able to drink coffee either!"
"Actually, I brought some with me, so I can have my last coffee time in life."
"Why did you bring it... I feel like an idiot for worrying about various things..."
"I read that it's important to carry food into dungeons! I got permission too!"
Alicia shot me a look that seemed to ask, "Is that true?" but since what I said wasn't wrong, I just nodded with a wry smile.
If I had permission, then it couldn't be helped.
"Alicia, let's drink some coffee and calm down."
"Yeah... please."
With a somewhat resigned expression, Alicia accepted the coffee poured from the magical bottle and began to drink.
Watching the two of them, I thought to myself.
These two could probably live quite normally even if they were thrown into the mountains of Brave Territory.
"Lagna, it seems there's only this path ahead. Should we continue?"
"There's no choice but to."
While taking a coffee break, we discussed our future course of action.
"I see..."
"If you step on a trap like this in a dungeon, it's usually game over."
I didn't say anything that might give them false hope.
Waiting for rescue was impossible, and due to the nature of dungeons, monsters would dissipate, making it impossible to survive by eating.
Though we seemed relaxed, we were actually in a super dangerous situation.
"So, what should we do?"
"We continue down the path in front of us, that's all."
If we were lucky, we might find a passage leading to either the upper or lower levels.
"Typically, teleportation traps often send you to the lowest level or to another room on the same floor, so it's important to remember where you were before teleporting."
"I see."
"But either way, if you step on one, you're dead, so be really careful. If this were a normal dungeon, Mariana would have killed us."
"S-Sorry! I just got too interested in the dungeon!"
As I bluntly conveyed the danger, Mariana turned pale.
She had calmed down after drinking coffee, so her tension returned.
"I want to say not to scare her too much, but this is definitely not a joking situation."
Dungeons that had been conquered were still few and far between, and they would mercilessly try to kill you as if they were the great outdoors.
Even so, I was going to go into the dungeon because it felt like an otherworldly experience.
"Lagna, are we going to be okay? You seem unusually calm."
"It seems this place was made by the Ancient Sage, and I think I read somewhere that if you defeat the guardian at the deepest part, you can return to the surface."
It was strange that I knew this, so I just brushed it off.
"You think so? Is it really okay?"
"I promised to protect you no matter what happens, so it'll be fine."
"That's true, but... um, thank you..."
"That's such a cheesy line, I'm envious. Good grief."
As Alicia blushed and looked away, and Mariana muttered something close to a defensive statement about being in a dungeon, we finally reached the deepest part of the dungeon.
The enormous space at the deepest part of the dungeon seemed to have been used for some grand ritual, resembling an ancient temple.
According to my knowledge, a Mithril Golem was supposed to be sitting in front of the massive door like a guardian.
If my knowledge was correct, that is.
"...Who are you?"
I muttered involuntarily.
The scene before me was completely different from what I remembered.
Something humanoid, wrapped in flames, was standing atop the melted Mithril Golem.
"Gihih...?"
The humanoid turned around in response to my voice and grinned.
In that instant, I felt an overwhelming killing intent.
Following my instincts, I deployed a barrier, and a torrent of flames was unleashed at us from the flaming humanoid, no, the scorching demon.
Gouuu!
The barrier blocked it, but the amount of magical energy wrapped in the flames was far too immense.
The flames that splattered to the side continued to burn, clinging to the floor.
"W-Wait, Lagna-san, could that be the guardian?!"
"I wonder."
Mariana was panicking, but I couldn't tell if it was the guardian either.
Mithril Golems were supposed to be highly resistant to magic and tough; they shouldn't be damaged by just any attack, yet it was melted.
This meant it was strong enough to dissolve it.
"Both of you, just stay back for now."
I couldn't let my guard down; the fire attribute was particularly troublesome.
Flames created by magic use magical energy as fuel, so the oxygen in this area wouldn't run out, but without resistance, just breathing the heated air could be fatal.
"Each of you should have defenses against fire... Wait, Alicia, are you okay?"
"Fire... n-no... I hate it..."
Alicia sat down, trembling in front of the blazing flames.
She placed her hand on her burn scar, nearly in a state of panic.
"Gya-ha-ha!"
The scorching demon clapped its hands and jumped around in delight as it watched her.
What the hell is that guy doing? More importantly, Alicia is in trouble.
"Alicia, look at me. Alicia, it's okay."
When I held her face to make her look at me, her gaze was directed towards the scattered flames around us.
I see, it's the flames.
Alicia had suffered severe burns after losing a duel.
Even if she pretended to be fine, the fear of defeat that resided within her was likely etched deep in her heart.
This was bad; once someone reached this point, even an average soldier couldn't return to the battlefield.
"Mariana, can you use water attribute defensive magic?"
"I can use Aqua Veil..."
I handed Alicia's trembling hand to Mariana and said,
"Deploy it with all your strength and stay by Alicia's side."
"Y-Yes!"
I asked the sage's apprentice to make sure they wouldn't get caught up in the aftermath of the battle.
"What about you, Lagna-san?"
As I finished the incantation and was enveloped in a water barrier with Alicia, I smiled at the anxious Mariana.
"I'm going to kill that thing."
Yes, I will kill it.
As I focused, the scorching demon seemed to understand my words, its twisted grin widening.
The swelling magical energy and the flames surrounding it grew even hotter, as if it was daring me to try.
"It's like the sun."
The heat dominated the space, and the towering pillars of the temple appeared to warp.
Magic that affected the surrounding environment was among the types I struggled with.
As I had told Alicia and the others, I would expend magical energy to block the heat produced.
A being with such powerful magical energy was, as far as I knew, a legendary monster like a dragon or Fenrir, or──a demon.
In the latter half of the story, it was the being to whom the villainous version of Alicia sold her soul for revenge.
Its characteristic was a monstrous humanoid form.
Demons from worlds different from this one could not manifest in this world without relying on humans, as they lacked a physical form.
When they did manifest, they took on a form heavily influenced by the individual who paid the price, resulting in the appearance of a demon like the one before me.
"I would appreciate it if you could tell me, who are you inside?"
The scorching demon maintained its twisted grin.
It was possible that it was taking the place of the demonized Alicia, so I wanted to know who was fulfilling that role, but it couldn't be helped.
"Well, I guess it doesn't matter; there's no point in talking to it."
Humans who made deals with demons had their desires greatly amplified, leading them to madness and losing their sanity.
"Gya-ha-ha!"
I didn't know what kind of madness it harbored, but its intent to kill was unmistakable.
I didn't know where it came from or who was behind it...
"I'll hold you responsible for triggering Alicia's trauma."
"Gya-ha!"
I drew the sword at my waist and took a stance. The demon leaped forward, closing the distance.
Goooon──!
Without a moment's pause in mid-air, the demon unleashed a massive fireball from one of its hands.
I slashed it in half, deploying a barrier on the cut surface of the fireball, forcing my way through and stepping forward.
"You're hiding behind that fireball, aren't you?"
I decapitated the demon, which had been hiding behind the fireball.
Using a distraction like that is basic; only an idiot would fall for it.
"Gya-hih!"
I felt the impact, but the scorching demon grabbed its floating head and quickly reattached it.
"So you don't die from that."
I had once fought a demon-possessed person from a neighboring country.
That one was also quite tenacious, but since it was human, it died when its head was cut off.
"Gya-ha-ha!"
How impressive, go ahead and try to kill me, the demon taunted as I readied my sword in a natural stance.
Well──.
"There's no real problem."
I shattered a small compressed barrier at my feet.
──Don!
With the force to shatter the dungeon floor, I instantly dove into the demon's embrace and pinned my sword to the massive door.
The gigantic door crumpled, revealing the shining Holy Artifact pendant inside.
"Gugigigi!?"
The demon's grinning face vanished at the speed that surpassed human understanding.
"Too careless."
To show any confidence against an opponent who wouldn't fall for my initial distraction was truly reckless.
If I wanted to outsmart it, I had to attack from outside its awareness with everything I had; that was the Brave Family way.
The best chance I had was when I decapitated it, wasn't it?
I thought it was capable, but the fight was below that of a Brave adventurer.
"Gya-ha-ha-ha! Foolish, you!"
Suddenly, the demon began to speak, and its magical power surged as its fiery body began to radiate even more heat.
The sword I had stabbed into it began to melt, and it seemed intent on burning me along with it.
"Gya-ha-ha-ha! Gya-ha! Gya...ha?"
However, the demon's boisterous laughter gradually lost its momentum.
As it stared at me, who was still unburned, its crazed face, with only black eyes and mouth, twisted as if it couldn't believe what it was seeing.
"Where's your confidence? At this rate, a dragon's breath would be hotter."
Laughing through my nose, I thrust my hand into the demon's chest.
No matter how monstrous it became, it was originally human, so crushing it from the inside shouldn't be a problem.
I thought that, but when I probed inside the demon's body, I found nothing.
The only thing that composed the demon's body was fire; it was as if it were empty.
"That's why it can survive even with its head cut off."
"Gih!"
The demon grinned again at my reaction.
This was a highly advanced puppet, and its true body was elsewhere.
"You may look confident, but once I figure out your source, it won't be a problem."
The barrier had the property of identifying what it allowed through, so it was adept at perceiving everything that touched it.
Therefore, I would investigate whose magical power this was.
"I won't let you off easily."
"Gih...Aaaaaaaaa!!"
As if sensing what I was about to do, the demon let out a piercing shriek while its magical power swelled.
Was it planning to self-destruct?
Judging by the swelling magical energy, the scale of the self-destruction would likely possess enough power to engulf this deepest part of the space.
"Tch, who the hell is controlling you?"
If it was fighting alone, it wouldn't be a problem, but the two behind me wouldn't be able to withstand it.
Even Aqua Veil, which was resistant to fire, would likely evaporate in this intensity.
"You bastard. Laughing from a safe distance."
I took a step back, holding the Holy Artifact pendant in one hand, glaring at the demon that had inflated like a balloon.
"I've grasped the sensation of your magical power, right? Next, I'll find your true body and kill it for sure."
I set up a barrier and told the now barely humanoid demon, and it grinned.
Then, it exploded.
An incomparably greater amount of heat than before began to incinerate the deepest part of the dungeon.
"This might be a bit hot? Well, a little burn is unavoidable."
The flames showed no signs of settling down for a while.
More than that, I regretted letting it escape, but I had firmly memorized the magical power it possessed.
I had also secured the pendant it desired, and as long as I kept brushing off the embers, I would eventually have to fight it again.
"Still, it's so bright. Next time, I should wear sunglasses while fighting..."
After the commotion in the dungeon, everything ended without any particular incidents.
Once the flames subsided, we conveniently returned to the entrance via the teleportation magic circle that had been set up in the innermost room.
Since we were the last to leave, it was not the examiners but the academy head, Volzeia, who was waiting for us.
Once he confirmed our safety, the old man silently walked away.
No, I think I heard him mutter something like, "Well done," in a voice only I could hear.
Did he intend to help us if something happened?
As a supporting character for the protagonist, he was likely always ready to assist in the main story.
It's okay; both of them are safe and have no external injuries from the aftermath of the battle.
However, I was a bit worried about Alicia, who had her trauma triggered.
Neither Mariana nor I knew the details of her duel.
Was there a connection between Alicia's burns and that fire?
Since Patricia, who holds the protagonist position, needs the pendant, one of the Holy Artifacts, to clear the story, it couldn't possibly be unrelated.
I genuinely wanted to help her overcome her trauma, but ultimately, only the person carrying it could confront their inner issues.
It was frustrating, but all I could do was be there for her.
But I believe in her; I know Alicia can overcome it.
She's such a strong woman that I can't help but admire her.
If it proves too difficult, I'll make her forget.
During the summer break, I'll give her a shocking experience at the Brave-style boot camp that will make her trauma seem insignificant.
I assure you, it's not in a lewd sense.
I think we're still too young for that kind of thing.
"Lagna-san, aren't you going to swim? It's a pool after all!"
"I'll do it later. It's fine to wait until Alicia arrives."
As I sat on a bench by the poolside, thinking about Alicia, Mariana appeared before me, wearing a competitive swimsuit.
The bottle-bottom glasses only accentuated her awkwardness, but being a former protagonist, her proportions were outstanding.
Due to the turmoil caused by Patricia, her status as a commoner was precarious without protection, but thanks to her thorough understanding of her position, Mariana had not attracted much hatred.
In fact, some students had begun to notice her charm, but due to their tendency to avoid nobles, they found it difficult to approach her, resulting in many hidden fans.
"Why are you friends with someone from Discarded Land? You don't have to deal with that guy."
"Hey, if you spread weird rumors, you'll get cursed."
"Do you know what happened to those who kept bothering him?"
"I heard they all had accidents. Isn't that just a rumor?"
"But that body has some serious scars; it looks like it could kill someone."
As a result, I somehow ended up receiving hatred from those guys.
They all looked at me with jealous eyes.
Sadly, making friends seemed like a distant dream for me.
"I'm going! If you guys are scared!"
"Going ahead is something a noble shouldn't do!"
"Bottle-bottom princess! How about some tea by the poolside?"
I could hear the shouts of the guys from a distance.
"Lagna-san, when do you think Alicia will arrive?"
Mariana, in contrast, completely ignored them.
"Um, am I not being called? From over there?"
"There's hardly anyone in this academy who would call me except for you and Alicia."
"Oh, I see..."
It was more accurate to say she wasn't ignoring them; she simply wasn't hearing them at all.
To say she wasn't hearing them was one thing, but to not even recognize them was quite impressive for someone with noble allergies.
Well, it's probably for the best that she didn't hear them. What's with "bottle-bottom princess"? I can't tell if it's a compliment or an insult.
"Where could Alicia be?"
"If she's not coming, then it's better that way; things are quite lively right now."
"Well, that's true..."
As we chatted, we watched the bustling pool from a distance.
"Patricia! You can't swim, right? Then let me teach you!"
"Edward... but I'm really not good with water... it's scary."
"Don't worry, I'm here with you. Now, slowly get into the water."
"Your Highness! Don't forget that I was the one who taught you how to swim! Leave swimming and water attribute magic to me, Russell Gran Cascade!"
